Let c_H ∈ HX^1(X_{MAJ_n}) be the canonical Hamming cocycle c_H(x,y) = d_{MAJ_n}(x,y) mod 2, and for each propagation R let T_R ∈ C_u^*[X_{MAJ_n}] be the indicator-banded Roe operator T_R(x,y) = 1[d_{MAJ_n}(x,y) ≤ R]. Then (i) the trace-pairing-derived invariant κ_n := sup_R log|⟨c_H, T_R⟩| / log(R) is monotone non-decreasing in n, and (ii) κ_n ≥ α · log n for some absolute α > 0, so that under asymptotic_completion the limit κ_∞ = lim κ_n is unbounded. Combined with axiom A1 (Coarse-KW link), this predicts depth(MAJ_n) = Ω(log n), and combined with A5 (Roe-index rigidity) the witness is stable under coarse equivalences induced by reduction_pullback.

If κ behaves like a true coarse invariant of an ultralimit, then along any natural function family it should be monotone and divergent whenever depth grows; Majority — whose formula depth is Θ(log n) — is the smallest non-trivial witness where the predicted κ-growth is detectable on tiny instances, but still nontrivial. The Hamming cocycle c_H is the simplest nontrivial coarse 1-cocycle (its δ-image is supported on triangle-defects, which vanish modulo 2 on the bipartite f^{-1}(0) ⊔ f^{-1}(1) partition), and indicator-banded T_R is the canonical Roe-controlled operator; the trace pairing reduces to a counting identity that scales with the propagation R, exactly the quantity that A1 forces to be polynomial in 2^depth.
